feedback: This candidate is valid and follows the evidence from iteration 0 (score 238.27). That baseline finished the oval 40% of the time with 0.75 line-loss events per run. The s-bend and slalom never finished: both ended off-track with about 2 line-loss events per run, and s-bend max_error reached 0.0635, above the 0.06 m limit. Losing the line on bends is the main failure, not running out of time. The changes target that failure directly: sensor x-coverage widened to ±0.03 m, the footprint enlarged to 16 mm, kp raised from 2.5 to 3.5 and kd from 0.3 to 0.6. The rationale keeps base_speed at 1.5, which iteration 0 shows is needed for the 3 s limit, and leaves ki, sensor_weights, line_loss and the wheel and mass geometry unchanged, so the race can attribute effects to coverage and gains. Nothing here is obviously broken, and no race of this candidate exists yet, so no outcome is claimed for it. Approve it to race now, since five action runs remain and it gives telemetry that the next critique needs. After the race, read the results as follows. If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom stay near 2, coverage alone did not fix the loss: reduce base_speed to about 1.3 and accept a slower finish. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, raise kd toward 0.8 before touching kp. If max_error stays under 0.06 but completion is still low, the limit is speed, so test base_speed 1.6 with the same gains.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom remain near 2 per run (iteration 0: 2.05 and 1.75), reduce base_speed from 1.5 to about 1.3 and keep the wider sensor array, because at 1.5 the robot loses the line before the coverage change can help.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 (iteration 0 oval: 0.2445 at kp 2.5, kd 0.3), raise kd from 0.6 to about 0.8 while keeping kp at 3.5.

If max_error stays below 0.06 and line losses drop but completion is still low with a long completion_time, test base_speed 1.6 with the same gains, because iteration 0 needed about 1.5 m/s to finish inside 3 s.
